Title: Unauthenticated test payment verification can mark payments completed and enroll users
Risk: Any caller who can hit the endpoint can force payment completion and course enrollment without auth or CSRF.
RecommendedFix: Delete the route entirely outside non-production environments and move any verification flow behind admin auth, signed requests, and audit logging.

Title: CSRF protection is broadly bypassed for quiz, topic-locking, admin payment verification, and manage-access admin actions
Risk: An attacker can target authenticated admins or tutors with forged cross-site requests because sensitive POST flows are effectively exempt or accepted leniently.
RecommendedFix: Revert to framework-default CSRF behavior, keep exemptions only for explicitly signed webhook endpoints, and require tests to prove admin flows work with real tokens.

Title: Debug and test endpoints expose session data, headers, cookies, users, and traces
Risk: These endpoints disclose internal state and increase the blast radius for session theft, reconnaissance, and privilege escalation.
RecommendedFix: Remove the routes and file from production codepaths or guard them behind local-only environment checks that fail closed.

Title: Quiz grading responses set wildcard CORS headers while the route is also CSRF-exempt
Risk: Cross-origin callers can interact with a sensitive grading endpoint more easily than intended, especially when paired with cookie-auth sessions and relaxed CSRF.
RecommendedFix: Remove manual Access-Control-Allow-Origin headers from controller responses and enforce CORS only from config for approved origins.

Title: Security headers and middleware are disabled on upload and video routes, with wildcard origin on profile images
Risk: Public file-serving routes bypass header protections and create inconsistent browser security posture around user-uploaded assets.
RecommendedFix: Serve files through a controlled controller or signed storage URLs, keep security headers enabled, and avoid wildcard origins on authenticated/user-generated assets.

Title: Student progress SQL queries reference columns and tables not present in the schema contract
Risk: Tutor progress, analytics, and export paths can fail at runtime because quiz_attempts does not define course_id, time_taken, or quiz_id in migrations and there is no quizzes migration in the inspected schema.
RecommendedFix: Refactor the service to derive course via topics, use duration_seconds consistently, remove quiz_id/quizzes dependencies, and add integration tests against a migrated database.

Title: Course and Topic models append multiple computed attributes that each trigger database work and can cause N+1 behavior during listing/serialization
Risk: Listing courses or topics for authenticated users can fan out into per-model count/progress queries and inflate response time under load.
RecommendedFix: Remove heavy accessors from global appends, compute view-specific aggregates in dedicated queries/services, and serialize only fields the page actually needs.

Title: QuizService fetches questions and then immediately runs a second existence query plus in-array filtering for the same records
Risk: This adds unnecessary database and PHP work on a hot quiz-generation path.
RecommendedFix: Collapse validation into the original query, rely on soft-delete or integrity constraints if needed, and avoid per-request duplicate existence checks.

Title: Cache services still use expensive random ordering and Redis key-pattern scans
Risk: ORDER BY RAND() becomes slow on larger question sets, while KEYS/pattern deletes can block Redis and degrade the whole platform under scale.
RecommendedFix: Replace RAND with indexed sampling/ID windows, replace KEYS usage with SCAN or explicit tag sets, and bound invalidation work per request.

Title: Tutor progress controller eagerly loads large relationship graphs and then discards them before calling raw SQL services
Risk: The endpoint pays for large object graphs, memory, and relationship hydration that are not returned to the caller.
RecommendedFix: Remove unused eager loading, authorize first, and fetch only the exact aggregates needed for the response.

Title: Question-count endpoint loads all questions into PHP memory just to count and group them
Risk: As question volume grows, this endpoint will scale poorly in memory and latency compared with database aggregation.
RecommendedFix: Replace the collection-based grouping with a SELECT source, COUNT(*) GROUP BY source query and return only aggregates.

Title: Operational commands are tightly coupled to Redis availability in a mysql+redis runtime profile
Evidence: Observed during audit: .env resolves to DB_CONNECTION=mysql, CACHE_STORE=redis, QUEUE_CONNECTION=redis; php artisan migrate:status failed in PhpRedisConnector
Risk: Routine deploy and maintenance commands can fail when Redis is degraded, reducing recovery options during incidents.
RecommendedFix: Make console/bootstrap paths resilient when cache/queue Redis is unavailable, provide safe fallbacks for health/migration commands, and add deploy-time smoke checks.
